title: 1998 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) angle \(C\) is a right angle and \(CB\gt CA.\) Point \(D\) is located on \(\overline{BC}\) so that angle \(CAD\) is twice angle \(DAB.\) If \(\frac{AC}{AD}=\frac{2}{3},\) then \(\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{m}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. Find \(m+n.\)

solutions.text: Let \(\angle DAB=\alpha.\) Since \(\frac{AC}{AD}=\cos2\alpha=\frac{2}{3},\) the identity for \(\cos2\alpha\) gives \(\tan\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt5}.\) Taking \(AC=1,\) \[ \begin{aligned} CD&=\tan2\alpha=\frac{\sqrt5}{2},\\ CB&=\tan3\alpha=\frac{7\sqrt5}{5}. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(BD=CB-CD=\frac{9\sqrt5}{10},\) and \(\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{5}{9}.\) Therefore \(m+n=14,\) so B is correct.
hints: Set \(AC=1\) and express \(CD\) and \(CB\) using \(\tan2\alpha\) and \(\tan3\alpha\)
